Tax on mobile phone services

ACT VII OF 1998
PUNJAB FINANCE
ACT, 1998
ACT VII OF 1998
An Act to levy and
enhance the rate of certain taxes, duties and fees in the Punjab
[Gazette of Punjab,
Extraordinary, 30th June, 1998]
No.Legis-2(26)/98/47, dated
30-6-1998.--The Punjab Finance Bill 1998, having been passed by the
Provincial Assembly of the Punjab on June 25, 1998 and assented to by the
Governor of the Punjab on June 30, 1998, is hereby published as an Act of the
Provincial Assembly of the Punjab.
8. Tax on mobile phone
services.--(1) There shall be levied and collected a tax on mobile phone
services at the rate of five per cent. of the actual bill of a consumer.
(2) The tax shall be payable by
the principal officer or person responsible on his behalf, of the organization
providing mobile phone services.
(3) Any person who fails to pay
the tax within the prescribed time shall, in addition to the amount of the tax
due, be liable to pay a penalty not exceeding the amount of tax payable.
(4) Any amount of the tax or
penalty imposed which remains unpaid shall be recoverable as arrears of land
revenue.
(5) The Government may make rules
for giving effect to the provisions of this section.

Tax on Luxury Clubs

ACT VII OF 1998
PUNJAB FINANCE
ACT, 1998
ACT VII OF 1998
An Act to levy and
enhance the rate of certain taxes, duties and fees in the Punjab
[Gazette of Punjab,
Extraordinary, 30th June, 1998]
No.Legis-2(26)/98/47, dated
30-6-1998.--The Punjab Finance Bill 1998, having been passed by the
Provincial Assembly of the Punjab on June 25, 1998 and assented to by the
Governor of the Punjab on June 30, 1998, is hereby published as an Act of the
Provincial Assembly of the Punjab.
9. Tax on Luxury Clubs.--(1)
There shall be levied and collected a tax on the amount paid by a member of a
luxury club to the club as admission fee and fixed annual or monthly
subscriptions, at the rate of ten per cent of the said amount.
(2) Subject to subsection (3), a
club which charges a minimum fixed monthly subscription of rupees three hundred
shall be treated as a luxury club.
(3) A club having only outdoor
sports facility with no additional indoor entertainment facilities for its
members will not be considered a luxury club.
(4) It would be the
responsibility of the management of the club to recover this tax alongwith
annual or monthly bills of the members of the club and a monthly invoice shall
be furnished by the management of the club to the Assessing Authority.
(5) Any luxury club which fails
to pay the tax within the prescribed time limit shall, in addition to the
amount of the tax, be liable to pay a penalty not exceeding the amount of the
tax due.
(6) Any amount of tax or penalty
imposed which remains unpaid shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
(7) The Government may make rules
for giving effect to the provisions of this section.
